result:
I reviewed the actual diff (not the self-report) plus dug into the linked compliance-tracker worktree to verify whether the backend endpoints this PROJEXA code calls actually exist.

**Verdict: reject** (tier1, so this only means "do not merge" — no human-signoff ambiguity since a reject leaves the PR open for a follow-up).

Key finding: the PROJEXA code itself is solid — consistent with existing proxy conventions, tsc-clean, and honest about the WhatsApp gap. But it depends on new compliance-tracker backend routes (drawings, veri-meetings, documents POST, permits POST/project-scoped GET) that only exist on an unmerged, no-PR branch in the other repo — verified directly against `origin/main` that those routes aren't there. Merging this now would ship two new sidebar items and two dialogs that fail in production, plus a permits list that silently falls back to unscoped data instead of erroring. Wrote the full reasoning and a recommended follow-up (merge the compliance-tracker PR first) to `review-verdict.json`.
